Feature: GTA 6 Made Me Want to Be a Good Guy (or Girl)

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (666 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pushsquare

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I’m playing a latest GTA game but I’m actually abiding by the traffic rules.
  • I’m playing a new GTA game but I’m clicking L3 and R3 to focus and targeting non-vitals.
  • I’m playing a latest GTA game but I’m actually opting to defuse the situation when an NPC gets mad at me.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I’m playing a latest GTA game but I’m actually abiding by the traffic rules.

I’m playing a new GTA game but I’m clicking L3 and R3 to focus and targeting non-vitals.

I’m playing a latest GTA game but I’m actually opting to defuse the situation when an NPC gets mad at me.

The more I reflect on my time with GTA 6, the more I realise this is not the GTA I necessarily grew up with, even though the carnage is always there bubbling beneath the surface.

That’s because just like GTA Vice City and GTA San Andreas, I do have the option to go on a reckless murdering spree.

I could stock up on grenades and sticky bombs and create chaos on a highway.

I could go to a beach and mow down innocent bystanders in a scene so gruesome it’d make Jack Thompson pass out.

I think this is the most remarkable thing about GTA 6 – it’s made me play differently to past titles, even though nothing has actually changed.

Industry observers note that so, why is this? Why am I choosing non-lethal as much as humanly possible, when the game allows me to go mental if I want to?

I think it’s a few reasons, personally.

Firstly, Jason and Lucia certainly aren’t saints by any stretch, but they just don’t seem like the type to go on a killing spree.

This isn’t the first GTA game to have protagonists with a slightly softer personality – GTA 4’s Niko immediately springs to mind, as does GTA 5’s Franklin.

But I think with romance being one of this game’s central themes, you really get to know these characters intimately.

It’s about the quiet moments, rubbing your partner’s feet in front of the TV.

It’s relatable – and if it’s relatable, then I think the vast, vast, vast majority of us are kind and caring to others.

Of course, this is still a video game and I racked up kills in the hundreds by the end of the campaign, but I never felt like I was doing it on purpose.

I made mistakes – I sometimes knocked cyclists clean into the air. I wouldn’t do that in real-life. But I did try to avoid these moments as much as possible here.

Industry observers note that one other wrinkle is that the realistic graphics mean the violence is pretty visceral. It’s fascinating to think how much criticism the PS2 trilogy got at the time, when it looks like a cartoon compared to this game.

I wouldn’t say the violence necessarily deterred me from being a cold-blooded killer, but I can see how it would affect others.

And also it’s a gameplay mechanic, right?

Behaving recklessly and showing no real care for other virtual life will alter your criminal profile, and change how the world reacts to you.

I ended up with a personality trait sitting somewhere between saint and sinner, but I think that’s probably normal as you’re still going to have to punch an NPC in the mouth from time-to-time.

I’m sure there’ll be people who see the GTA series as more of an arcade game than the life sim it’s become in GTA 6, and there’ll be many who don’t like this change.

Industry observers note that for me, I’m fascinated by how Rockstar subtly convinced me to play a GTA game like it’s not a GTA game. And I didn’t even really notice it until recently.

That’s just one of the title’s many, many achievements – and one of the reasons why it’s now the highest rated game of all time.

Sources indicate that have you found you’re playing GTA 6 in a less aggressive manner than past titles? Are you taking care on the road and picking the non-lethal option wherever possible? Be a bit nicer to the Leonida natives in the comments section below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I don't want to write about video games any more, I want to deliver milk in the countryside and hang out with a cow and quirky people! Sorry, what, there's a game all about that called Milki Delivery that came out today? Alright, I'll write about video games again, especially when they look as charming as this one does.

The stakes at play in Milki Delivery are very low (as are the steaks, no butchery to be found here, only one very sweet looking cow I couldn't possibly slaughter). You play as Neha, and she's made a promise to her pet cow, the titular Milki, that you'll find her a friend (I think this is a world where there aren't any cows left; yikes!). To do that, all you have to do is deliver her milk! Accept because this is an adventure game, you'll have to help out a few folks along the way.

Industry observers note that it's a game very much about the journey, as when riding about this lush and bright countryside, you might find a group of cats that just need a little taste of that sweet creamy juice you've got. Or maybe you have some rope that a farmer needs to wrassle up some sheep. Sometimes you'll have to get a bit more involved with the various people you meet, but predominantly, you'll be delivering milk to folks who need it.

According to recent reports, getting around the place is quite simple too, you plot out your path ahead of time and let the game take you as it's all mouse driven. A relaxed experience to be sure, but the game's art is just so delightful to look at, I'm quite enticed by the idea of just slowing down and enjoying some pretty pictures and making friends along the way. You can make different kinds of milk, too, just be feeding Milki different ingredients. Not how that works in real life, but now I kind of wish it was.

In any case, Milki Delivery is out now, and you can pick it up on Steam.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that update [Fri 20th Nov 2026, 10:02pm]: GTA 6 publisher Take-Two is now reporting that day one sales reached $3.79 billion USD, while also selling 32.5 million units pre-release. The $3.79 billion figure is based on "tech giant estimates".

Here's a bit of their statement:.

Recent findings suggest that "Rockstar Games, a label of Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. (NASDAQ: TTWO), is proud to announce that Grand Theft Auto VI day one retail sales reached $3.79 billion, setting a new record for entertainment across any medium, and becoming the biggest entertainment launch in history.".

"Achieving a near perfect score of 99 on Metacritic and resounding critical acclaim, Grand Theft Auto VI sold 32.5 million units pre-release, a upcoming record across all platforms.".

Original Story: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 has reportedly smashed all sorts of records within 24 hours of launch, and it's off to a great start on Xbox Series consoles.

As shared by GTA 6 Countdown, GTA 6 has launched to a near-perfect 99 score on Metacritic (151 reviews), apparently sold 24.5m copies in under 24 hours, and seen 2 million Xbox players take a trip to Newly introduced Zealand to play the game early.

Sensor Tower's sales tracker also estimates $2.36bn (£1.8bn) in revenue from GTA 6 sales, with the console split mostly in favour of PS5, at a 75% to 25% share over Xbox. Still, the data suggests Xbox still took a whopping $588m from 6.15m units sold.

GTA 6 dominated Twitch viewership too, with 50m hours watched and 3.3m viewers during its busiest hour, beating the livestreaming site's previous record (held by Hogwarts Legacy at 1.2m) by more than double.

Beyond all the massive numbers we're chucking your way, we've also spotted a lot of praise for the Xbox Series S version of the game. Whilst Digital Foundry was hit-and-miss on the report, the general response online is majorly positive.

It's good news, then, to finally put to bed the lingering question of whether GTA 6 would run well enough on Xbox Series S consoles. Judging by IGN's comparison, it's not all that different of an experience to Sony's flagship PS5 Pro.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that whether you're looking for GTA 6 safe codes for story missions or just for grabbing some quick cash around Leonida, you can find over 50 safes in GTA 6. Some of these are locked with codes and others can be broken into, with the former typically offering larger rewards.Unfortunately, aside from safes you come across in story missions and major side quests, most safe codes are randomized, but I can at least help you there by guiding you on how to obtain them. Either way, you've got a few options at your disposal when it comes to cracking safes in GTA 6, so here's everything you need to know.

There are two methods of getting GTA 6 safe codes:.

Sources indicate that which you'll need depends on the location, but by using your Focus by pressing down on L3 and R3/LS and RS, you can highlight the location of the safe code if there is one. If you can't see one, you probably need to threaten the staff by holding down the LT/L2 button and then press X/Square to threaten. Eventually, the threaten option will turn into a 'Safe code?' option, as seen in the image above. The Avery Pawn Shop GTA 6 safe code is an example of one of these, so why not use that to try it out.Alternatively, safes that require a code can be blown open using sticky bombs. These are only unlocked once you reach the Credit Checked mission in Chapter 3, but as I've explained in my dedicated guide to getting into the Kingpin Bowling safe in GTA 6, there are a few you can pick up at the alley - and presumably other places around the GTA 6 map - before you unlock them at Ammu-Nation.

These are the set GTA 6 safe codes that are the same for every player:.

Aside from the 0420 safe code that's given to you in Chapter 1, there are three main safe codes you'll need when gathering funds in GTA 6, and they're all related to the Kolt gang in Port Gellhorn. All three codes are found in the same place, Brooks Boatworks, but since they're set, you can use them from our list above without having to go looking for them. This won't save you a lot of trouble, though, as you'll still have to get past the gang in all three locations anyway.

There then appear to be a handful of other safe codes that aren't randomized, due to the nature of how you find the code, and I'll add those to the list above as I find them.

Breaking: Former GTA 4 and Red Dead boss thinks "we are one Toy Story moment away" from people accepting gen-AI in game development in the West

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (536 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ben Feder, the former Take-Two CEO who oversaw the launch of massive hits like Grand Theft Auto 4, Red Dead Redemption, Borderlands, and BioShock during his tenure, believes the resistance against gen-AI in games will vanish once the games industry has its 'Toy Story moment'.
  • Industry observers note that "When animation went from hand-drawn to computer animation, there was a massive wall of resistance," Feder told The Game Business.
  • Sources indicate that feder argued that the success of Toy Story ended the resistance against computer-generated animation, and the same could happen to games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ben Feder, the former Take-Two CEO who oversaw the launch of massive hits like Grand Theft Auto 4, Red Dead Redemption, Borderlands, and BioShock during his tenure, believes the resistance against gen-AI in games will vanish once the games industry has its 'Toy Story moment'.

Industry observers note that "When animation went from hand-drawn to computer animation, there was a massive wall of resistance," Feder told The Game Business. "People didn't think it looked good. Then Pixar launched Toy Story. They created a movie that not only was awesome, but used computer-generated animation and chose a subject matter that made the most of it, and did an amazing job with it.".

Sources indicate that feder argued that the success of Toy Story ended the resistance against computer-generated animation, and the same could happen to games. Feder added, "My own view is that we are one Toy Story moment away from consumer acceptance of AI in video games in the West. In the East, they've already accepted it.".

Feder, who presently heads up venture capital fund Tirta Ventures, is investing in AI-first games. He, however, doesn't necessarily believe AI will reduce development costs, but that it also offers other advantages that could help game makers keep up with shifting consumer tastes.

"A lot of incumbents think about AI as a way of reducing costs, which it is," Feder mentioned. "I query whether it will actually reduce costs, or will it just make games bigger for the same cost? But we're more interested in what AI can do to radically change gameplay.".

According to recent reports, feder views gen-AI simply as newly introduced technology that allows developers to do things they couldn't before. He likened it to Unreal Engine's instancing technology, which allowed Fortnite and other battle royale games to support 100+ players in a single server.

"That's question number one as we think about what we invest in: Was this possible before AI?" Feder said of his VC firm's strategy. "And when AI gets better, does the game get better? That's harder for an incumbent to focus on, because they deploy a lot of capital, have enormous advantages in terms of distribution, capital, and IP, and all of that needs to be protected.".

There's been enormous pushback from players, developers and pundits against the use of gen-AI in games. Even so, more and more studios have revealed using some gen-AI during development, such as to assist with coding. More broadly, gen-AI adoption is on the rise across the industry, with a recent report estimating 40 percent of developers are using it.

Some development studios, such as Fortnite maker Epic Games, have doubled down on the use of gen-AI in game development. Epic is even more bullish on gen-AI in its Unreal Engine, which the tech giant is presently transforming into an engine that's almost entirely driven by gen-AI and LLMs. Consumer sentiment remains sour, however, and the perception of the tool is not helped by the number of 'AI slop' games taking over Steam's storefront, the 'enshittification' of fan wikis, or the link AI seems to have to the unprecedented wave of layoffs that has shaken the industry over the past two years.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that nvidia's board have indicated that they aren't about to do a major u-turn and reappoint recently resigned CEO Jensen Huang, following his departure after multiple alleged instances of extramarital cavorting were reported by the press. Since his exit last week, Huang has indicated he'd be open to making such a return, were it deemed best for both the company and AMERICA.

"On November 12th, our board of directors announced that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the tech giant's code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms, Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as president, CEO, and board member," Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones said during an investors call on November 17th (thanks, Percieving Calls Gamer). "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.".

That last bit seems likely to have been said with the intention of quieting down some of the speculation around a Huang return that's been bubbling away since he removed his bum from the black and green throne and that the exec embraced in a statement put out yesterday. "I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life," he wrote. "I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the board’s independent investigation.

According to recent reports, "Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. Nvidia is a once-in-a-generation company. If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO.".

It has been revealed that for now at least, it seems leather jacketed GPUperman will not be triumphantly flying back into his former post amid a wave of corporate and patriotic fervour. Likely as part of continued efforts to reassure moneyfolk that they won't be making negative headlines again soon following Huang's departure, Nvidia's board announced yesterday that they're establishing a "new standing committee responsible for board-level oversight of the organization’s national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management". One of Huang's alleged affairs was with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. The Chinese government have denied the accusations of espionage.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress is at the moment serving as Nvidia's interim CEO while the organization's board searches for a permanent sexy leather jacket man replacement.

According to recent reports, I think we all knew it was going to be big, but this big? Rockstar has unveiled that GTA 6 sold a staggering 32.5 million copies during its preload period, setting a “latest record across all platforms”.

That number is likely higher by now, because the press release’s wording implies it’s not counting launch day sales into the above total, which are guaranteed to be plentiful. (It’s only going to keep rising through Thanksgiving and Christmas, too.).

Industry observers note that rockstar says the game generated a frankly mind-boggling $3.79 billion on day one, making it the biggest entertainment launch in history. Estimates claim it cost about $1 billion to make.

It’s also eager to point out that the title is now the highest-rated game of all-time as well, with its near-perfect 99 Metacritic score nudging the N64 version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time aside.

According to recent reports, “It is with immense gratitude that we enter a latest chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of GTA 6. We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you.”.

The dev didn’t specify how sales were split between systems, but the expectation is the PS5 version sold best, with some estimates pegging it at around 75% of the total.

Sony was the primary marketing partner of the game, and promoted the fact it “plays best on PS5” (even though testing highlights it’s broadly identical to the Xbox Series X version on base hardware).

Recent findings suggest that this is just the beginning for GTA 6, of course, with no word on Rockstar’s prepares for the next iteration of GTA Online just yet. The game is also expected to launch on PC in 2027 as well.

If you’re one of the 32.5 million people playing, don’t forget to check out our GTA 6 guide for tons of information on the game.

Blizzard suspends World of Warcraft: Forever gold exploit abusers, puts trading blocks on their accounts and removes ill-gotten funds for good measure

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (655 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, players who abused World of Warcraft: Forever's Blackmaw Hold unintended gold farm, which allowed a small minority of players to hoard thousands of gold in a few days, have drawn the ire of WoW publisher, Blizzard.
  • For those unaware, the World of Warcraft: Forever community was greatly alarmed by this gold farm, which had players clear the same non-elite enemies from the new late game dungeon, Blackmaw Hold.
  • There was much speculation on what would happen to those who participated in this exploit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, players who abused World of Warcraft: Forever's Blackmaw Hold unintended gold farm, which allowed a small minority of players to hoard thousands of gold in a few days, have drawn the ire of WoW publisher, Blizzard. Suspensions have been issued, trade locks have been put on accounts, and ill-gotten gold is being seized.

For those unaware, the World of Warcraft: Forever community was greatly alarmed by this gold farm, which had players clear the same non-elite enemies from the new late game dungeon, Blackmaw Hold. By swiftly clearing select mobs with area-of-effect damage, players would loot upwards of 100 raw gold an hour. This exploit, clearly not intentional, was nonetheless farmed until Blizzard hotfixed it earlier in the week.

There was much speculation on what would happen to those who participated in this exploit. That speculation would come to an end late last night with an official statement from the World of Warcraft: Forever development team.

"As players continue their journey into WoW Forever’s higher-level content, we are closely monitoring the game economy to ensure that gold sources and costs are well balanced," the statement reads. "Finding efficient farming spots has always been part of the game, and is how most players have earned their epic mounts since 2004. When a single location proves so lucrative that it overshadows all other sources, we generally adjust it to bring it in line with the rest.".

It goes on to explain the nature of the bug that made this gold farm possible, before reassuring those who may have accidentally benefited from some extra cash from their regular runs of Blackmaw Hold they have nothing to worry about. The same cannot be said for those who took advantage of the situation.

Recent findings suggest that "Players who simply ran Blackmaw Hold a few times and benefited organically from the extra loot did nothing wrong, and no one should worry that they’re putting their account at risk if they accidentally benefit from a bug," it continues. "But there were a couple hundred players worldwide who recognized that this was unintended and spent significant time exclusively farming that group of enemies.

According to recent reports, "Yesterday, we put an economy lock on their accounts to prevent broader impact to the game economy while we investigated the extent of the exploitative gains, including gold earned by vendoring bugged drops. Today, we are in the process of removing all such gold earned, as well as applying account suspensions to significant abusers.".

The post concludes by thanking players for their feedback on the matter, and a final warning: "As always, we advise all players to refrain from abusing game mechanics that are clearly unintended. We will continue to take action against intentional abuse.".

This decision certainly sets the precedent moving forward with World of Warcraft: Forever that such exploits won't be tolerated, and rolling back the wealth of those who made out of Blackmaw Hold like bandits is a good measure that should prevent continuous damage.

Inevitably the exploit would have had some impact, specifically in those days prior to trading blocks being put in place. While the gold on the exploiter's accounts may be removed, any purchases they made on the in-game auction house will have affected others through buying and selling goods with ample funds.

Those who were suspended temporarily will be able to regain access to the game by the time the first wave of raids come out in December, so it very much feels like a firm slap on the wrist in that regard. Even so, given the establishment of punishments for such behavior, one can only wonder if future events will come with harsher penalties.

World of Warcraft: Forever, despite this small economic roadbump, is proving exceptionally popular for Blizzard. It's already broken records for the series, and has impressed players so far with its revamping of the classic MMO.

#86465. Industry News: Despite being £61.7 million in debt, bankrupt MindsEye devs Build a Rocket Boy are splurging on legal action against "a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews"

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1282 w)

Business & Policy 📈 Bullish 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Despite being £61.7 million in debt, bankrupt MindsEye devs Build a Rocket Boy are splurging on legal action against "a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews"

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1282 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Freshly published bankruptcy documents for perennially troubled MindsEye developer Build A Rocket Boy have spelled out the scale of the company's debt, with around £61.7 million owed to creditors.
  • According to recent reports, BARB's largest debt by far is the roughly £36.5 million owed to NetEase, publishers of Marvel Rivals.
  • Build a Rocket Boy have been on a journey, it's fair to say.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Freshly published bankruptcy documents for perennially troubled MindsEye developer Build A Rocket Boy have spelled out the scale of the company's debt, with around £61.7 million owed to creditors. The documents also touch on founder Leslie Benzies and CEO Mark Gerhard's claims that MindsEye is the victim of an organised sabotage campaign. The company's leaders have apparently taken out even more loans in order to fund legal action against the suspected perpetrators, with the promise of a healthy payout. I'm not holding my breath.

According to recent reports, BARB's largest debt by far is the roughly £36.5 million owed to NetEase, publishers of Marvel Rivals. Asset manager Diameter Capital Partners are the second largest external creditor, having loaned BARB around £4.25 million. A further $19 million is owed to "group undertakings" – "group undertakings" meaning debts to parent companies, subsidiaries or fellow subsidiaries. Studio founder Benzies, meanwhile, is owed £1,158,167.05. Given that Benzies has been repeatedly accused of torpedoing MindsEye's fortunes by way of disruptive micro-management, I'm not sure many BARB staff would agree that he really deserves his million quid back at this stage, but that's what it notes on paper. Smaller IOUs include £10,434.11 for Amazon Web Services, £634.36 for Unity, and a mighty £19.90 for OpenAI.

Build a Rocket Boy have been on a journey, it's fair to say. Revealed in 2023, their flagship project MindsEye is a filmic GTA-ish action shooter initially billed as a full-fat demo for Everywhere, a game creation platform comparable to Roblox. MindsEye struggled to compel us before launch and did not find its people on release, with poor sales leading to layoffs even as BARB leadership insisted they could revive the game's fortunes.

The same leadership were subsequently accused by their own staff of "disastrously" mishandling the redundancies and enforcing "unbearable" crunch. Unionised BARB employees have now taken management to court for installing alleged surveillance software on their work PCs. The game's publishers Io Interactive noped out of the picture in March this year. Meanwhile, Benzies and Gerhard have thrown around accusations of a sinister espionage and sabotage campaign, carried out by unspecified perpetrators. They made a sort of revenge fantasy DLC pack about it, which our own Mark Warren characterised as we-already-have-Hitman-at-home. The bankruptcy documents shed more light on these twists and turns. According to the administrators, BARB were "funded mainly by equity investment from institutional, strategic and venture capital investors over several funding rounds, including a $110m Series D round in 2023." This followed a £32 million investment in 2020, as reported by GI. The organization grew significantly during MindsEye's creation to around 500 UK and overseas employees. According to a group income statement, the company posted sequential operating losses of £47.5 million for the period ending September 30th, 2025, and £63.1 million for the year ending December 2024. The administrator proposals document also devotes some time to the aforesaid allegations of sabotage. "The directors formed the view that the game's commercial prospects may have been adversely affected by a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews and commentary," it reads. "The directors subsequently received information which they considered suggested the involvement of a number of third parties in organising and funding such activity and commenced litigation against some of those parties. The directors have indicated that such claims may be substantial in value, although the extent of any recovery remains uncertain and will be dependent upon the outcome of ongoing investigations, legal proceedings and asset recovery actions." A later section vaguely alludes to the sum BARB leadership hope to recover. "Prior to the Joint Administrators' appointment, the Company had undertaken detailed investigations and had commenced litigation against several third parties, with the assistance of the Company's former legal advisers, Brandsmiths, in connection with matters described earlier in the Proposals," the doc reads. "The Joint Administrators consider the litigation potentially to be the largest asset of the Administration." The document goes on that BARB management have "sought financial support from third party investors to fund the anticipated legal costs and expenses associated with the litigation", with some of these funding agreements already executed. "Further executed agreements and associated funding contributions are expected to be received, shortly, and a substantial litigation fund is anticipated to arise," it continues. The Joint Administrators are "currently engaging in the on-going litigation, progressing the funding arrangements entered into by the Company, and have assessed the merits of pursuing the litigation". They will liaise with relevant parties to "determine the most appropriate strategy for preserving and, where appropriate, realising value from this potential asset for the benefit of creditors and other stakeholders." The doc doesn't name who, exactly, is being taken to court. As far as I'm aware, it isn't us. Anyway, it's good to know that the company who owe over £60 million are taking on more debt in order to pursue a histrionic grievance for which they have yet to supply any real evidence whatsoever.

I Didn’t Expect The X Files And David Duchovny To Be A Key Part Of JLo’s Famous Green Dress Story

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s not difficult to imagine why Jennifer Lopez went viral when turned up to the 2000 Grammys in her green dress with a super low-plunging neckline.
  • Most people know that JLo’s green Versace “jungle dress” is such a substantial celebrity fashion moment that it led to the creation of Google Images.
  • I was nominated that night and I wore it to The Grammys, and I was very excited.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s not difficult to imagine why Jennifer Lopez went viral when turned up to the 2000 Grammys in her green dress with a super low-plunging neckline. (That dress looked like it was made for her!) But did you know that The X-Files and David Duchovny also played a role in why it’s such a moment, too? I sure didn’t!

Most people know that JLo’s green Versace “jungle dress” is such a substantial celebrity fashion moment that it led to the creation of Google Images. It caused such a high volume of online interest that Google, which was only two years old at the time, decided it was time to engineer the feature. Although The X-Files of it all? I had no idea. Lopez told the story of the dress recently, saying this about it:.

I was nominated that night and I wore it to The Grammys, and I was very excited. It was just one of those moments… [I didn’t know it was going to be something], I just picked the best dress on the rack.

Industry observers note that JLo didn’t set out to create some internet-shattering moment when she stepped out at the Grammys. She just wanted to look good. As she added on Friends Keep Secrets:.

In a recent development, when I walked out on stage you could see it on my face because there was like swell in the room of [applause]. And, I was just like, ‘What’s happening?’ And then, David Duchovny was with me, and he was like, ‘This is the first time in years I know nobody’s looking at me.’.

It has been revealed that so Lopez presented an award with David Duchovny, who was one of the biggest names in TV at the time, who was in his seventh season of the show. In the clip she talked about how at the time Duchovny couldn’t go anywhere without being recognized and had recently filed a multi-million dollar lawsuit against 20th Century Fox. Here they are together:.

In a recent development, I can imagine Duchovny feeling perhaps like the heavily covered lawsuit might be the elephant in the room when he was going to The Grammys that night. However, when he was paired with JLo on the night of the green dress, all eyes were on her. As JLo continued:.

In a recent development, the thing is I walked out on stage and it was like a bodysuit, right? And it had the material, very just flowy material, like chiffon. And when I walked out, it blew open. The moment was the thing. The wind blew, the people started, he had the perfect line. It wasn’t scripted.

Recent findings suggest that it sounds like the room absolutely lost it when JLo hit the stage with Duchovny, and his line complimented it all like a cherry on top. Even though the moment happened over twenty-five years ago, it has remained relevant over the years with a number of pop culture moments. The most recent one has to be when Mika Abdalla wore the dress during a scene in Off Campus. (The show’s costume designer shouted out how the dress stayed on if you’re as curious as I was).

And then, Rachel Zoe also put on the dress for a magazine cover shoot, too. Last year, the original model who first wore the Versace piece on the runway, Amber Valletta, also slipped back into the chiffon dress. Will JLo ever top this look? We don’t know, but you can see her in The JLO Show, streaming with a Paramount+ subscription on November 26.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Now she's into covering YA television and movies, and plenty of horror. Word webslinger. All her writing should be read in Sarah Connor’s Terminator 2 voice over.

It has been revealed that rockstar's lengthy credits reveal just how massive the GTA 6 song list truly is, but you don't start the game with every radio station unlocked. Leonida has two secret playlists (both needed for 100% completion), and neither is particularly hard to unlock once you know where to look.

Industry observers note that the Sniper of La Perle, Kodak Black's 22-track playlist, becomes available as soon as you scan four posters around La Perle at TWA Ponya Tattoo, Drip Drops, Aunt Zola's Soul Food, and the Jack of Hearts nightclub. Then there's The Vault Radio, which only requires you to scan a single poster at the nightclub of the same name.

Sources indicate that the shops automatically marked themselves on my map as I drove around La Perle and Crosstown, but I've included screenshots highlighting their specific locations in Vice City's Haitian district. Once you arrive at one, Jason or Lucia's phone should alert you to something nearby you can scan with a notification from the Waink It app.

In a recent development, look right as soon as you enter the parlor. There's a Sniper of Perle poster on the small table by the door.

You'll find another Sniper of Perle poster lying on the cash register counter.

The Sniper of Perle poster is immediately to the left as you enter, on a corkboard in front of the cash register.

Head upstairs to the second floor and enter the Jack of Hearts recording studio. Pass through the lobby and into the control room, then you'll see the Sniper of Perle poster lying on the table beside a fan.

It has been revealed that once you arrive at the nightclub, head through the entrance corridor and look at the back wall. The poster is right there, and one quick scan is all it takes to unlock The Vault's playlist.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

New Zealand's tourism board has taken advantage of all the excitement surrounding Grand Theft Auto 6's launch, as hordes of players who've changed their Xbox timezones to that of the world's second best rugby team (sorry) to jump into the game early.

"One perk of seeing the sun first? Getting GTA 6 first too," reads a post on the Fresh Zealand tourist board's Instagram account: PureNewZealand. "We heard a few of you are trying the New Zealand trick to join us. We get it, and we'd love to have you." The post also includes a video of folks looking at all the natural beauty of New Zealand, presumably before they all look themselves indoors to play the video game, alongside the caption: "life, because we're getting GTA 6 first.".

Industry observers note that for those unaware, Xbox owners have been swapping their console time zones for years to New Zealand in order to take advantage of the region's access to games before anywhere else in the world. When games have, let's say, a worldwide release time of midnight across all nations, those living in New Zealand are able to jump in first as a result.

Industry observers note that microsoft has for years been happy to let this practice continue on its platform, and as such a sort of cultural norm about hopping on a digital plane for a game's release has been established. If you want guidance, we have a guide on how to pull off the GTA 6 New Zealand trick yourself which can walk you through it.

Sources indicate that if you aren't keen on doing so for whatever reason, you can find a breakdown of all the global launch times for GTA 6 too. If you want one final run through on what to expect from Rockstar's big release last minute, our Everything We Know about Grand Theft Auto 6 page should set you right for good measure.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Publisher PLAYISM and developer viv have announced Saihate Station: Twilight Edition, a Switch version of the 2D exploration horror adventure game including the base game and downloadable content “Twilight Railway,” as well as two mini-games. It will launch on March 25, 2027 worldwide with English, Japanese, Korean, Traditional Chinese, and Simplified Chinese language support. A physical edition will be available in Japan for 8,800 yen.

Saihate Station first introduced for PC via Steam on March 7, 2025. The downloadable content “Twilight Railway” launched on April 18, 2025.

Here is an overview of the game, via PLAYISM:.

Sources indicate that since its release in March 2025, this 2D exploration horror adventure game has recorded a cumulative series total of 1.6 million downloads, an exceptional achievement for an indie free game, and continues to receive passionate support from fans in Japan and abroad. Now it is finally coming to Nintendo Switch!

Saihate Station: Twilight Edition includes the main game, the downloadable content “Twilight Railway,” and two mini-games, all in one package.

“After falling asleep on the last train, I woke up in a bizarre place called Saihate Station…”.

Recent findings suggest that haru Akinashi is a self-effacing office worker who lacks confidence and fails at everything he tries. Having slept through his stop on the last train, he finds himself trapped in a bizarre place called Saihate Station, where gruesome supernatural phenomena occur.

Shion Tatsunami is his complete opposite: a cheerful, talented colleague and former friend—happens to be there as well, and the two promise to work together to return home.

Their interactions are awkward at first, given the estrangement, but with each problem they overcome together, Haru recalls their former friendship, and their bond grows stronger than before.

Then, the truth of the world closes in.

The main game features four multiple-ending story routes. The ending branches based on fluctuations in Haru’s “dependency level,” which changes according to the player’s actions.

Industry observers note that starting November 20, pre-orders for the physical edition will begin sequentially at retailers in Japan. As a first-print bonus, a “shaka-shaka acrylic stand keychain” featuring a train and character motif will be included. A limited edition featuring a special box with an “exclusive newly drawn mini-game book” and a “Haru-Shion handkerchief” is also planned. Bonuses and limited editions are available in limited quantities, so please place your pre-order early.

GTA 6's Ultimate Edition features a collection of different items and pre-order bonuses, including vehicles, weapons, and cosmetics. These are unlocked at different points in the story, and some need to be collected from locations around the map. This GTA 6 guide includes step-by-step instructions on how to collect them and when they become available.

There are 15 extra packs included if you pre-ordered GTA 6's Ultimate Edition. This is where you find them:.

Sources indicate that here's the location on your map. You can also set a marker to the exact store by selecting the Style > Souvenir & Swimwear tabs, as below:.

You'll find the Goodtime Gear items inside the shop, on mannequins just left of the entrance:.

The Ultimate Edition exclusive items are marked with a blue tab, as shown:.

Recent findings suggest that you can find One-Eyed Willie's Auto Shop just off SR-27 in North Leonard County starting from Chapter 1. It looks like this from the outside:.

And here's a map view to help direct you to the right spot:.

You can set a waypoint using the menu tabs Vehicles > Mod Shops:.

Drive in to the mod shop to find exclusive paint jobs and body work, many of which are exclusive to the Ultimate Edition:.

It has been revealed that you'll need to have visited South Vice-Dale County before the PTT Youngin$ Illegal Goods robberies unlock starting from Chapter 1. Once you have, you'll find two robberies in and around SW 13th St and El Joven Blvd in Southside.

Here's how one looks from the outside:.

The Rideout Custom Mod Shop is located in Crosstown, Vice City, Vice-Dale County. Here's what it looks like outside:.

Shortly after collecting your '67 Vapid Dominator, you'll receive a text message on your phone from Wyman telling you about a classic car you can recover and tune up.

This triggers a new chain of missions where you must scan scrap cars for Wyman to repair.

You can find Wyman's Classic Car Locations through the link.

Go to any Ammunation store around Leonidas and select Manage Weapons at the Weapon Locker, like below:.

Your Vintage Vice City Pack pre-order bonus will become available shortly after you arrive in Vice City. A marker will appear on your map telling you to visit the familiar Ocean View Hotel in Vice Beach, telling you to pick up your '55 Vapid Stanier, which can be located like below:.

The car is unlocked, and once you get inside you'll automatically receive the Shore Court garage as well as fresh clothes in your wardrobe. A prompt will inform you of this:.

Industry observers note that you can collect your Shitzu Squalo beginning Chapter 4, docked near to Atlantic Ave, Washington Beach, Vice Beach, Vice-Dale County. Here's where you'll find it:.

Sources indicate that you'll get a notification about the '95 Grotti Cheetah upon completing Honest Abe in Chapter 5. Follow the waypoint to Pegassi Residences and go through the main front door, as shown:.

Go inside the main entrance and use the lift opposite the entrance:.

Head down to Parking B1 in the lift:.

Your '95 Grotti Cheetah will be parked up and waiting for you to get inside:.

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6's Ultimate Edition costs $99.99/£89.99/€99.99. The Standard Edition costs $79.99/£69.99/€79.99.

Yes, I personally think GTA 6's Ultimate Edition is worth it, but it really depends how excited you are for the game and whether you want to get the most out of it.

All of the additional Mod Shops and Stores exclusive to the Ultimate Edition, along with their unique inventory, means you're really adding a lot of cosmetic and personalisation options to the title with the Ultimate Edition.

If you're not the type of player that looks to dress up Jason and Lucia and fiddle with their vehicles, then you may not find value in this.

But it's worth adding that the Classic Car Collection, which adds collectibles quests involving Wyman, are also exclusive to the Ultimate Edition.

You can still enjoy GTA 6 to its fullest without paying for the Ultimate Edition, but you'll get much more out of the game if you do.

Yes, the Ultimate Edition Upgrade can be purchased from the PS Store at any time for $20.00/£20.00/€20.00 and will automatically add all of the extra content to your game once installed.

You'll need to buy the Ultimate Edition Upgrade if you purchase a physical edition of GTA 6, as this content isn't included with the retail release.

According to recent reports, if you've followed this guide carefully, then you should now have collected all of your Ultimate Edition items and pre-order bonuses in GTA 6. Congratulations for getting them all!

Remember, you can refer to our GTA 6 guide for a lot more info on the game, including collectibles, walkthroughs, and much more.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As you've probably heard, GTA 6 is out on consoles this week and targeting 30 FPS on that hardware.
  • The wait for confirmation of a PC version continues, then, and it looks like that might well be the only chance people get to play the crime sandbox at 60fps, with Rockstar having confirmed that higher frame rate modes aren't en-route to even the most beefy of consoles.
  • Speaking to Kotaku, GTA 6's devs made clear optional 60 or 40fps performance modes aren't on the way, even for the more powerful Pro variant of the PS5.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As you've probably heard, GTA 6 is out on consoles this week and targeting 30 FPS on that hardware. Despite reports claiming one may not be far away, there's still no official word on a PC port, hence why we've not got a review that delves deep into analysis of just how central to the experience the smell reaction system is.

The wait for confirmation of a PC version continues, then, and it looks like that might well be the only chance people get to play the crime sandbox at 60fps, with Rockstar having confirmed that higher frame rate modes aren't en-route to even the most beefy of consoles.

Speaking to Kotaku, GTA 6's devs made clear optional 60 or 40fps performance modes aren't on the way, even for the more powerful Pro variant of the PS5.

"Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination. On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR)," Rockstar technology production director Marc Chambers put it. "The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game’s visual fidelity. While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates.".

So, there you go. The consoles just ain't got that dog in 'em. One would think, then, that being able to run GTA 6 in all its glory at higher frame rates will likely be a selling point for that PC port that's assumed to be on the way. Whether the average PC owner's graphics card and other bits will have the horses to deliver a smooth 60 is another question, and an especially pertinent one given the ongoing RAM crisis has made upgrading certain aspects of your setup ludicrously expensive.

If it requires a 5090 at a minimum, I guess those of us with less than absolute cutting edge cards will just have to keep playing Sleeping Dogs until the AI bubble bursts.

Slay the Spire 2 is one of this year's best selling games despite only being available on PC, and its players are "obsessed"

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (473 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, one million copies for each month on sale, it seems.
  • That's according to estimates by Alinea Analytics industry analyst Rhys Elliott, who revealed in a LinkedIn post that those sales translate to $157.6m (~£119.6m) in revenue for the small studio.
  • Slay the Spire 2 is now the sixth best-selling 2026 release across Steam, PlayStation and Xbox.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, one million copies for each month on sale, it seems. Slay the Spire 2, Mega Crit's roguelike deckbuilder, is estimated to have sold 7.9m copies since its release in Steam Early Access in March.

That's according to estimates by Alinea Analytics industry analyst Rhys Elliott, who revealed in a LinkedIn post that those sales translate to $157.6m (~£119.6m) in revenue for the small studio.

Slay the Spire 2 is now the sixth best-selling 2026 release across Steam, PlayStation and Xbox. That is notable, as the game is only out on Steam, meaning it has sold enough copies to outpace games on platforms it's not even available on.

In a recent development, we already knew Slay the Spire 2 was one of the year's biggest releases. In its first week on sale, the game sold over 3m copies. It promptly became March's top-selling game on Steam, beating blockbuster competition in Crimson Desert and Resident Evil Requiem. Slay the Spire 2, alongside other indie titles such as Meccha Chameleon, have helped Steam deliver another record year of revenue.

It was such a hit, even, that other indie developers felt it negatively impacted sales of their own games. Mewgenics maker Edmund McMillen recently told Eurogamer "it sucked everybody out". "The same players who liked Mewgenics, they were Slay The Spire players. So they all went woosh and right over," McMillen mentioned.

Slay the Spire 2 has been consistently popular with players, too, and that popularity has seemingly continued. Elliott noted the game never fell below 2.5 million active players each month since March.

Slay the Spire 2's loyal following also meant that the recently released beta patch, which added a new character, was enough to bring back millions of players. Despite only being available for players who opt into the beta branch of the game, Slay the Spire 2 more than doubled its daily active customers to reach its highest daily player count in six months.

"Simply put: Slay the Spire 2 players are obsessed," wrote Elliott. "And it's not just a niche group of dedicated players, either. The average play time is nearly 84 hours, sure. But zooming out, 1.9 million folks have played for over 100 hours.".

Incidentally, nearly 100,000 players bought the game but never played it, which Elliott added could explain the discrepancy between player numbers and copies sold.

Looking ahead, Slay the Spire 2's road to version 1.0 is expected to be long, with several features and gameplay additions still in the works. Then there are the console ports, which have yet to be unveiled, but are very much expected.

In Eurogamer's Slay the Spire 2 early access review, Bertie Purchese called it "a deceptively familiar sequel" whose confident design and smart new additions build on what made the original work so well.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that scott, of course, directed Blade Runner and is an executive producer on Blade Runner 2099.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Blade Runner 2099 is set 80 years after the events of 1982 sci-fi classic Blade Runner, but despite the Replicant-filled world undergoing some radical changes in the intervening decades, the Prime Video show's creator turned to Ridley Scott for clarification on a number of canon questions.

Recent findings suggest that scott, of course, directed Blade Runner and is an executive producer on Blade Runner 2099. So when 2099 showrunner Silka Luisa had questions about the history of the cyberpunk world, there was only one place to turn. "He's such an idol for me. It was like meeting a rock star," Luisa tells GamesRadar+. "He had so much insight into the first film, because so much of it is off-screen your imagination just takes over, but there's a lot of open questions intentionally, right? It's very ambiguous.

According to recent reports, "So when I went to go write," Luisa continues. "I realized that the canon is not concrete, and so it's hard to build on top of that foundation when you're not sure if what you're saying is accurate or not. And so, what was really helpful with Ridley was being able to ask him: What I thought this meant – is this correct? What did you think Off-world was? Where did you think the Replicants came from? Tell me about Tyrell; how did you imagine him? I mean, just as a fan, they're the questions you would be dying to have answered. But also from a practical sense, as a writer, I just needed to know. I needed the Bible for our show, and that was Ridley.".

Recent findings suggest that this makes sense – Scott is perhaps the only person to have played a major creative role in all three live-action Blade Runner projects, as he was also an executive producer on 2017's Denis Villeneuve-directed Blade Runner 2049. And unlike Star Wars, Game of Thrones, the MCU, and many storytelling sandboxes, there is no one person or group that is the arbiter of canon in the Blade Runner universe. Instead, it's up to the creators of each individual project to forge ahead, which could become a problem when looking back.

Recent findings suggest that it's safe to say, then, that Blade Runner 2099 will have one eye on the past, while looking to the future. Starring Michelle Yeoh as Replicant Olwen, and Hunter Schafer as a human Cora, Blade Runner 2099 is set in the aftermath of a Replicant revolt that saw synthetic humans rise to power and humans subjugated. Bad news for Cora, who must go undercover at the LAPD to win freedom for her and her brother. The final trailer is out now.

While it's not ignoring canon, we do know that Blade Runner 2099 is "not directly connected" to Blade Runner 2049, and won't directly pick up on the events of that movie, as it's designed to "stand alone". And while a second season of Blade Runner 2099 is unlikely, as the 8-episode show is already being billed as a "limited series", franchise producers Alcon Entertainment have suggested a AAA Blade Runner video game is in the works.

Sources indicate that blade Runner 2099 releases in full on Prime Video on November 25. For more, here's our Blade Runner timeline, and our breakdown of the most exciting upcoming TV shows.

Chronicles: Medieval devs Raw Power are bankrupt, but their sandbox RPG lives on at a new studio co-founded by Satisfactory devs Coffee Stain

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (367 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Goat Simulator and Satisfactory outfit Coffee Stain Group have bought the intellectual property rights and assets for Chronicles: Medieval, the Tom Hardy-garnished strategy RPG that was originally in development at now-bankrupt Raw Power Games.
  • In development since 2022, and slated for Steam early access release in 2027, Chronicles: Medieval is a game about building vast armies of men in metal hats and horrifying doublets, then fighting alongside them in real time.
  • In a recent development, the original devs included people who worked on The Witcher 3, Total War, and Crusader Kings III, which may not surprise you from the foregoing descriptions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Goat Simulator and Satisfactory outfit Coffee Stain Group have bought the intellectual property rights and assets for Chronicles: Medieval, the Tom Hardy-garnished strategy RPG that was originally in development at now-bankrupt Raw Power Games. The game will now be made by a new developer, owned 25% by a few former Raw Power devs and 75% by Coffee Stain. Coffee Stain will fund the game's on-going development.

In development since 2022, and slated for Steam early access release in 2027, Chronicles: Medieval is a game about building vast armies of men in metal hats and horrifying doublets, then fighting alongside them in real time. It sees you positioning archers behind spears and finessing your cavalry flanking actions, all the while occupying a fleshy human body that can be hacked and stabbed. It's set during the Hundred Years' War between England and France over the 14th and 15th centuries, and gives you a volatile sandbox world of warring factions and patrols.

In a recent development, the original devs included people who worked on The Witcher 3, Total War, and Crusader Kings III, which may not surprise you from the foregoing descriptions. It's not entirely clear who has made the leap to Coffee Stain's newly founded studio.

Industry observers note that raw Power declared bankruptcy on 30th October, subsequently calling on players to help them find funding. During the bankruptcy proceedings, Coffee Stain successfully bid 36.75 million Danish Krone for Chronicles: Medieval, which comes to around four million pounds or 5.4 million dollars. According to CEO Anton Westbergh the project "ticks many of the boxes that we believe to be fundamental for a great game, and we think it has a good chance of becoming a strong long-term IP for the group." The game yet sits at 26th on SteamDB's most wishlisted, despite Raw Power's funding troubles.

Gaming doesn't want for simulations of shrieking feudal folk, but Medieval has a certain swagger, even when you remove Tom Hardy from the picture (and you should - he only ever voiced that one trailer). Here's hoping the newly introduced team can find their feet under Coffee Stain, and that whoever hasn't made the transition finds good work elsewhere.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that last night, it was revealed that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33's lead narrative designer, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, won a BAFTA Breakthrough US award for her contribution to the hit 2025 game, which made history after winning 12 Game Award nominations last year. In the aftermath of her win, Svedberg-Yen dropped a pretty substantial bombshell: she's no longer with the game's developer, Sandfall Interactive.

It has been revealed that "No, I left Sandfall in July, after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition," she told Gamesbeat when asked if she's still with the company. "We've parted ways." As to what Svedberg-Yen is doing next, she offered a cryptic answer, including talk of writing "my own projects, my own stories". She also discussed another project she's set her sights on: establishing a fund to help mentor and grow a new generation of video game narrative designers.

In a recent development, "One of the initiatives I want to build is a narrative investment fund to focus on narrative-focused game creators, trying to bridge the gap between the seed stage and going to publishers," she explained, noting her background working in finance and how that dovetails nicely with her more recent experience as a narrative lead. "This is the chicken and egg question a lot of people face. To get money from publishers you need a demo, but to make a demo you need money. To get money you have to go to publishers. That’s an area where I would like to help a lot of these smaller creatives to get that seed funding so they can, in a way, de-risk themselves in the eyes of bigger investors.".

Recent findings suggest that her motivation for this initiative? Simply, she wants to change how the industry works. "I've discovered that quite a lot of studios don’t really know how to think about narrative, or how to integrate it into their pipelines and their processes. They tend to think it's a very narrow thing, when in fact it can influence all aspects. Part of this would also be an incubation program to help these studios develop those narrative foundations.".

"The strongest feeling in me right now for 2027 is I want to help," she added later. "That sounds so cheesy and idealistic. I always cringe at myself for saying it. But I don't know how else to say it and be truthful. I want to help in some way, help the industry.".

Sandfall Interactive previously said its guiding "North Star" will always be its "own personal taste", and what the team enjoys.She noted that she didn't think the studio would bow to pressure from fans to do more of the same, but instead be guided by what it thinks is best for itself, and for the series. "I've seen too many TV shows and books be swayed trying to please a lot of people, and in the process you end up losing the heart of what's there," she noted.

It has been revealed that we know that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is "not the end" of the franchise, and it seems that whatever happens next, it'll have at least a little bit of Svedberg-Yen's creativity instilled in it. I wish her the best for whatever her next step is.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, in a first substantial update since acquiring SteamDB from its founders back in September, the owners of Nexus Mods have outlined some fresh additions coming to , the two sides in the deal have unveiled some additions coming to the community-run backend database. Affiliate links aimed at providing options to help folks find the cheapest price for a game and a new tab dedicated to the mods Nexus host for a game are incoming, as work on behind-the-scenes improvements continues.

"We're now a couple of months in since [the takeover] announcement, so I thought it was about time we shared a quick patch on what we've been working on behind the scenes, along with a few changes you'll start to see rolling out over the coming weeks," Victor Folmann, CEO of Nexus Mods owners Chosen wrote in a blog post on SteamDB.

Sources indicate that there are two main new features he pointed to that you'll notice popping up on SteamDB soon. The first is one that anyone could have seen coming, a new tab on each moddable game's page that shows off some mods hosted for it on Nexus Mods and a host of modding-related data. "The new tab will help you discover mods for games you're browsing on SteamDB, making it easier to see whether a game has an active modding community and explore what it has to offer," Fomann wrote. "For now, we'll only be showing mods from Nexus Mods, as we already have access to that wealth of modding data, making it a straightforward starting point for this new feature.

"We appreciate that some of you might be wondering why we're not including Steam Workshop, too. It's certainly something we'd be open to exploring as we develop the feature further, along with other modding sources. With that in mind, if you run a modding website and would be interested in having your community's mods included, we'd love to hear from you.".

Sources indicate that that seems perfectly fine, but the other incoming feature's a bit more controversial given SteamDB's historically not been all about the money. "One thing we've seen people ask for is an easier way to find the cheapest place to buy a game, and we're now working on making that possible," Folmann wrote. "We'll be introducing affiliate links to authorised game retailers, giving you more options when looking for the best available price on a game.

"We recognise that introducing affiliate links may raise some concerns, so we want to be clear about how they'll work. First and foremost, as I mentioned, we'll only feature authorised retailers; we will not be including grey-market resellers. We've also made a deliberate decision about how prices are displayed: retailers will be ordered by the cheapest available price in your currency, not by whichever retailer offers us the highest affiliate commission. If a retailer doesn't offer pricing in your currency, we'll still show deals in other currencies provided they are available in your region.".

In a recent development, folmann was clear in the initial announcement of the takeover that Nexus Mods' bosses would be actively looking into ways SteamDB could make more money to sustain itself, so the addition of these links isn't out of the blue either. Whether SteamDB regulars agree that they're a "lighter-touch" way of earning the site some cash without detracting from the traditional experience of using it is another matter. I'll need to see how I feel once I've actually navigated a few pages with the links in as part of looking up stuff about games, but my first instinct is that as long as the pages don't end up revolving around the links and it's still easy to get to the info you want without interacting with them, I probably won't be too put out.

In a recent development, beyond those tweaks, Folmann mentioned "improvements to how updates are tested before they go live" and how swiftly the team can react to issues have been among the less obvious work going on behind the scenes. "We're still in the early stages of what we want to achieve, and there's plenty more work we need to do and would like to work on," he wrote in closing.

Folmann and co only took over Nexus Mods in June last year, making them still relatively new custodians of both it and SteamDB.

It turns out there is a reason why that significant match was cut from the film and moved into the credits.

According to recent reports, now, even though they took a “week” to film the fight between Rocky and Creed for this movie, it was eventually cut…kind of. Ultimately, the scene was moved to the credits. So, why did that happen? Well, director Peter Farrelly told me the match was actually supposed to be the end of I Play Rocky. However, a massive realization about the stairs scene changed his mind, as he recalled during an interview with CinemaBlend:.

Industry observers note that and by the way, it wasn't originally supposed to be over the end credits. It was supposed to be the end of the movie. But when you get in an editing room, as good as the script is, you have to let the movie find its way. And when he goes up the top of those stairs [and raises his arms up], there was such a high watching it that you couldn't get there again.

While the director was very open about this being the right call with me, he also admitted that it took him a while to fully accept that. It took a long time to film the fight, and it’s such an iconic moment from Rocky. However, he eventually came to the conclusion that they had to move it to the credits:.

Industry observers note that like even though we took a lot of time making that fight and doing it, you will never get that high again. You're not going to feel it. And so I indicated it to a few people in the editing room. They go, ‘You should end on the top of the stairs.’ I was like, ‘No, I took a week. I took a week to shoot the fight. I'm not cutting the fight.’ And it took me a couple weeks to finally realize I have to cut the fight. It's got to end on the stairs.

I know I was a bit shocked not to see the fight prominently featured in the movie, when so many of the other scenes are. However, I did think it was a cool surprise to cut it into the credits, and it served as a full-circle moment to the scene where we watch Anthony Ippolito’s Sylvester Stallone and Stephan James’ Carl Weathers train for the fight.

Speaking of Ippolito and James, they, like Stallone and Weathers, trained and learned how to box for this movie. That means they took a few punches too. When I asked the Sly actor about filming the fight between Rocky and Creed, he said:.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 is already enormously successful, having enjoyed "the biggest entertainment launch in history". But the current games industry is such that some Rockstar developers are still concerned about being laid off in the wake of its release. Writing for the Guardian prior to GTA 6's launch, Rockstar animation programmer Nestor Uriarte explained that although there is "no indication that layoffs are coming" it nonetheless "claims a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off.".

According to recent reports, it might sound odd for the developers of such a hugely successful game to be worried about losing their jobs, but layoffs don't just occur when games or companies struggle commercially. A common cause of layoffs in the games industry is companies trying to reduce overheads after a game has launched, as the studio switches from full production to post-release support for their current game and planning for the next one.

According to recent reports, it's partly why the industry seems to be in a constant, rolling state of layoffs, even when games appear to sell well. This matter was recently addressed by Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, the lead writer of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. Svedberg-Yen, who left Sandfall Interactive in July, claimed that the problem is exacerbated by an imbalance in who benefits financially when a game like Grand Theft Auto 6 launches.

"99 Metacritic score. Multiple award nominations before it even released. Massive sales and player engagement. Incredible amounts of tangible and intangible value creation. Yet the team is worried about layoffs," Svedberg-Yen wrote in an Instagram post. "So, who receives the lion's share of the profits from their labor? Not the vast majority of the creative team.".

Svedberg-Yen pointed out that this is "one of the issues that happens when the people creating the value do not receive a proportionate amount of that value," adding that "In finance, we call that value extraction.".

Sources indicate that svedberg-Yen also commented on the Rockstar team's ongoing efforts to unionise, with the team in the process of voting on whether or not it wants a union. If successful, the Rockstar Game Workers Union would become the biggest in the UK's gaming sector.

"I sincerely hope the Rockstar team is successful in unionizing," Svedberg-Yen wrote. "Layoffs during lulls in development cycles would work a lot better if teams were properly paid for the value they create, not just one-time, but throughout the life of the thing they created.".

Xbox alone has cut thousands of jobs, with more planned going into January 2027. Most recently, Firaxis, owned by GTA 6 publisher Take Two Interactive, reportedly laid off a third of its staff earlier this week as it works on a new XCOM.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, GTA 6 rolls out on console today.
  • In an article supporting this month's union vote at Rockstar North, one of the game's animation programmers argues that "workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.".
  • It has been revealed that the animation programmer in question is Nestor Uriarte, writing in The Guardian's Comment Is Free section.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, GTA 6 rolls out on console today. It's widely expected to sell more copies than main character Lucia Caminos has skin pores, more copies than there are words even in Eurogamer's five-star review, which I believe Chris Tapsell has written specifically to exhaust and destroy such neurones as I have remaining. And yet, staff at Rockstar Games are apparently worrying about being laid off, as development winds down and investors start to bicker about Line Going Up Even More.

In an article supporting this month's union vote at Rockstar North, one of the game's animation programmers argues that "workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.".

It has been revealed that the animation programmer in question is Nestor Uriarte, writing in The Guardian's Comment Is Free section. Following some personal reflections on his time at the studio, he calls on other Rockstar devs to get behind the union, describing it as both "a huge step forward" for a company that has previously faced allegations of "crunch culture", and a win for UK game developers at large. "What happens here could open the door for other workers across the UK to imagine an alternative future for the industry – one in which workers’ voices are taken into account more," Uriarte writes.

The vote at Rockstar North will run till 26th November, and could give rise to a union spanning over 1600 developers, according to umbrella organisation the Independent Workers of Great Britain. If that comes to pass, it would make the Rockstar union the largest recognised videogame developer union in the UK.

It comes as the company and a group of fired workers await the result of an employment tribunal battle over alleged "union-busting". Rockstar has accused the workers in question of "gross misconduct" and a breach of confidentiality by means of a union Discord server. Amongst other things, the legal brawl has revealed that Rockstar had a mole on that server for two and a half years, prior to the firings.

As for the prospect of further job losses, after GTA 6 goes on sale, Uriarte cites a wave of mass layoffs across the industry that has affected the creators of even commercially successful games like Battlefield 6 and Netflix's FIFA World Cup.

Sources indicate that "After the big day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it’s hard not to worry about what the future holds," he writes. "Studios across the industry have been slashing huge portions of their workforces, with an estimated 24,000 roles axed globally over the last two years. It notes a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off. But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.".

Sources indicate that the obvious context here is that GTA 6 has been a massively expensive production, with a development team headcount in the thousands. While one could accuse Uriarte of fear-mongering, I do find it hard to believe that executives at parent company Take-Two aren't weighing up some timely "down-sizing" right now. In general, videogame companies have a long tradition of axing the books once a game has been shipped, despite arguments that keeping experienced teams intact often pays off. In Rockstar's case, however, it's also worth bearing in mind that the GTA 6 rolling out this week is only part of the package. There's also the hazy prospect of the next incarnation of GTA Online, which – going by GTA 5 sales – will be a money spinner for many years, and will require a sizeable staff to maintain. Oh, and of course there's the PC version.

Sources indicate that echoing many peers, Uriarte also argues in his piece that it's key to unionise now in order to negotiate proper protection against generative AI cost-cutting initiatives. "The rapid emergence of AI is transforming how studios work and raising fundamental questions about the future of our industry," he continues. "Across the sector, the skills that workers spend years developing risk being devalued as their creative work is replaced by AI.

In a recent development, "Rockstar has stated it is committed to preserving jobs and it has been clear that our games will continue to be made by people," Urirarte concedes. "But with recognition we’d have a seat at the table to manage this industry-wide transition together.".
